newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end down, no action on PM's speech.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end down, no action on PM's speech.

text.p: The Greek equities ended the week slightly down, reflecting a neutral view towards Prime Minister Costas Simitis's policy speech on Thursday and correcting part of yesterday's rise, market analysts said.

"The market took a neutral stance towards the premier's policy speech," said Marilena Vassiloglou, said fund managers at ABN-AMRO mutual funds. "The speech did not help the bourse find direction and all eyes are on the 1997 budget."
The draft 1997 budget will be presented in November and Deputy Finance Minister Nickos Chrystodoulakis told reporters that the figures will be finalised in early November.

The chairman of the council of economic advisors, Yannis Stournaras, told Reuters that the government's top priority was to achieve a general government budget deficit to GDP ratio of 7.6 percent at any cost.
Vassiloglou said the prospects for the bourse were still positive but press reports about changes in the tax laws could nervousness could give rise to nervous trading while awaiting the 1997 budget.
Other market watchers said the drop of the benchmark index was a correction to its sharp rise in late session on Thursday.
"Today's drop is a correction to the bourse's sharp rise in late session on Thursday," said John Dimitriou, head of research at National Securities SA.
The Athens general share index closed 0.24 percent, or 2.27 points lower at 960.87 from Thursday's 963.14 close after opening at 954.19 points.
Turnover was lower at 5.84 billion drachmas on volume of 5.65 million shares.

Gainers traced decliners 86 to 105 with 46 issues unchanged on 237 traded. Banks fell 0.92 percent, industrials up 0.17 percent and construction ended lower 0.09 percent. Small-caps fell 1.00 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 541-559 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom OTEr.AT, the underlying, was unchanged at 4,055 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was at 197.90-208.30 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1051.1.
The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of sic banking stocks was quoted at $12.33-$13.33. The strike price was at $99.6.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 4,771-5,062 drachmas at the close. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
